speaker: Poet (maṅgala)
question: What is first worshipped?
premises: Homage to the world-formed, beyond the world.
To ever-divine-shining, self with unending power.
inference: The maṅgala names its object twice: the formed world transcended, the shining self whose power does not end.

speaker: Poet (identity)
question: Who are you, who am I?
premises: You alone are you; I alone am I; you alone are; I am not at all.
I and you as both are not: where homage, homage, homage.
inference: Identity and non-identity both refused: neither you alone nor I alone, nor both — only homage where the question lands.

speaker: Poet (seeking)
question: What is found inside?
premises: Sought inside the body by me always — you as self, and never seen is the self.
Whatever is seen is you alone, that.
inference: Seeking finds no self to see: whatever is seen is you alone — the sought turns out to be the seer.

speaker: Poet (recognition)
question: What does the devotee declare?
premises: Of your devotee who well knows your form, now again.
Having seen you as the self's form: to you homage, to me homage.
inference: Recognition declared both ways: seen as self, homage goes to you and to me — knower and known each honored.

speaker: Poet (method-question)
question: What finesse remains?
premises: What going-finesse, what to be done, thus, from the root.
Of yours, made of your magic power: by what, in what, whence the dissolving.
inference: Method questioned to its root: given your magic-nature, what instrument, what place, what origin could dissolving have.

speaker: Poet (non-duality)
question: Is there duality?
premises: I, you; you, I — thus: no duality of us anywhere.
Only the wish to grasp samādhi: abiding of difference is just that.
inference: Non-duality asserted, difference explained away: what looks like abiding difference is only the wish to grasp samādhi.

speaker: Poet (speech)
question: Where do words go?
premises: You-I and so-on, so endless, ever in you, never find a place.
Words, then — whence the world.
inference: Speech finds no room in you: if even I-and-you-talk cannot stay, whence a world of words.
uncertainties: Print variant so yamityādi nūnaṃ tāni noted; edition so'nantāni kept.

speaker: Poet (enough)
question: What is enough?
premises: Enough of difference-talk: from chewing the sap of devotion to you.
All this is one, at peace — even to say so is shy.
inference: Enough of talking difference: devotion chewed to sap leaves all as one, at peace — and even saying so is shy.

speaker: Poet (expansion)
question: What when you expand, what when you withdraw?
premises: Your own form expanding — you and I and the whole world.
Born its withdrawal — neither you nor I nor world indeed.
inference: Expansion holds all three; withdrawal holds none: being and nonbeing of you, me, world turn on your play.

speaker: Poet (actor)
question: Who shines like an actor yet stays partless?
premises: Waking-dream-deep-sleep and the rest, holding as own rays.
By own will you shine like an actor — partless, yet in truth.
inference: States held as own rays: shining by own will like an actor, yet partless in truth.
uncertainties: Print naTavan kept byte-true (probable slip for naṭavat actor-like); gloss follows sense.
